keywords.def: a woman who stays home to take care of her children and manage the household
change an earlier decision you made or opinion you had
not able to be fixed or brought to a satisfactory resolution

a period in which two groups who are arguing can try to improve the situation before taking further action, or, an agreed length of time in which someone can decide not to buy something they have agreed to buy
to become involved in a difficult situation in order to improve it

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: This is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English.
sentences.zh: 这里是BBC英语教学的《6 Minute English》节目。

sentences.en: I’m Phil. And I’m Georgie. In the words of a famous 1960s pop song, ‘breaking up is hard to do’.
sentences.zh: 我是Phil。我是Georgie。用20世纪60年代一首流行名曲的话说，“分手很难”。

sentences.en: Divorce, when a married couple who no longer want to be together separate, can be one of life’s toughest experiences.
sentences.zh: 离婚是指不再想在一起的已婚夫妇分居，这可能是人生中最艰难的经历之一。

sentences.en: During the 1990s, divorce rates in Europe and America were the highest in the world, with almost half of all marriages ending in divorce.
sentences.zh: 在20世纪90年代，欧洲和美洲的离婚率是世界上最高的，几乎有一半的婚姻以离婚告终。

sentences.en: But since then, the trend has reversed and divorce rates in the West have slowed.
sentences.zh: 但自那以后，这一趋势发生了逆转，西方国家的离婚率有所放缓。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, however, the number of couples divorcing in other parts of the world is on the rise.
sentences.zh: 然而与此同时，世界其他地区正在离婚的夫妇数量却在上升。

sentences.en: In this programme we’ll be hearing how divorce is talked about in different countries.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将聆听不同国家是如何讨论离婚的。

sentences.en: But first, I have a question for you, Georgie.
sentences.zh: 但首先，Georgie，我有一个问题要问你。

sentences.en: In Britain, one day of the year in particular is known by divorce lawyers and relationship counsellors as ‘Divorce Day’, but which day is it?
sentences.zh: 在英国，一年中的特定一天被离婚律师和婚姻顾问称为“离婚日”，那到底是哪一天呢？

sentences.en: a) Christmas Day? b) the first Monday of the new year? or, c) Midsummer’s Day, the 24th of June?
sentences.zh: a) 圣诞节？ b) 新年的第一个星期年月？ 还是 c) 夏至，即6月24日？

sentences.en: Hmm, I think ‘Divorce Day’ is the first Monday of the year.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我认为“离婚日”是新年的第一个星期一。

sentences.en: OK, Georgie. We’ll find out if that’s the correct answer later in the programme.
sentences.zh: 好的，Georgie。我们将在节目后期揭晓这是否是正确答案。

sentences.en: Getting married very young, and differences between partners’ backgrounds or interests are two common causes for couples to grow apart.
sentences.zh: 结婚很早，以及伴侣背景或兴趣的差异，是导致夫妻渐行渐远的两个常见原因。

sentences.en: Today, Marina Adshade is a professor at the University of British Columbia who studies the economics of sex and relationships, but her life has a very different beginning, as she told BBC World Service programme, The Global Story:
sentences.zh: 今天，Marina Adshade是不列颠哥伦比亚大学的一位教授，她研究性别与关系的经济学，但她的人生有着截然不同的起点，正如她对BBC世界服务节目《The Global Story》所说的那样：

sentences.en: I married really young, I had no education, I married somebody who is older than me, who had a lot of education and our relationship worked well for a while.
sentences.zh: 我结婚很早，没有受过什么教育，我嫁给了一个比我年长、受过很高教育的人，我们的关系在一段时间内进行得很顺利。

sentences.en: And then in my late 20s I decided to go back to school, I no longer wanted to be a stay-at-home mother which was what I was doing in my 20s, and that change in our situation for us just became completely unresolvable.
sentences.zh: 然后在快到20多岁的时候，我决定重返校园，我不再想做一个全职妈妈，而那正是我20多岁时在做的事情，我们处境的这种改变对我们来说变得完全无法解决。

sentences.en: And I think this is true for a lot of marriages because people’s situation changes over their lives, maybe they want children then maybe they change their minds.
sentences.zh: 我认为这对很多婚姻来说都是如此，因为人们的处境在他们的一生中会发生变化，也许他们想要孩子，然后又可能会改变主意。

sentences.en: Marina started her married life as a stay-at-home mum – a woman who stays home to take care of the children and manage the household.
sentences.zh: Marina的婚姻生活是从全职妈妈开始的——全职妈妈是指呆在家里照顾孩子和打理家务的女性。

sentences.en: Marina married an older man, and although their relationship started well, over time they developed different ideas about what they wanted from life.
sentences.zh: Marina嫁给了一个年长的男人，尽管他们的关系一开始很好，但随着时间的推移，他们对生活的要求产生了不同的想法。

sentences.en: Marina and her husband changed their minds - they changed an earlier decision they had made.
sentences.zh: Marina和她的丈夫改变了主意——他们改变了之前做出的决定。

sentences.en: Growing apart is one of the most frequently given reasons for divorce, and eventually Marina and her husband’s problems became unresolvable – not able to be fixed or satisfactorily ended.
sentences.zh: 渐行渐远是离婚最常给出的原因之一，最终Marina和她丈夫的问题变得无法解决——无法解决或圆满结束。

sentences.en: Marina’s experience is typical of someone who finds themself trapped in a marriage that no longer works.
sentences.zh: Marina的经历非常典型，就像那些发现自己被困在不再幸福的婚姻中的人一样。

sentences.en: Yet unfortunately, due to economic or emotional reasons, many people stay trapped.
sentences.zh: 然而不幸的是，由于经济或情感原因，许多人仍然被困在其中。

sentences.en: So, what can be done? Now, some countries are looking to the authorities, rather than the couple themselves, for a solution.
sentences.zh: 那么，能做些什么呢？现在，一些国家正在向官方寻求解决方案，而不是靠夫妻双方自己。

sentences.en: Here, Lucy Hockings, presenter of BBC World Service’s The Global Story and divorce counsellor, Joanna Gosling, discuss a new strategy being used in China: There was an interesting thing they did in China where they introduced this cooling-off period.
sentences.zh: 在这里，BBC世界服务节目《The Global Story》的主持人Lucy Hockings和婚姻顾问Joanna Gosling讨论了中国正在采用的一项新策略：他们在中国做了一件有趣的事情，就是引入了所谓的“冷静期”。

sentences.en: So, the government enforced this. Does that work when the government intervenes in a situation like this and makes people behave or do things in a certain way?
sentences.zh: 所以，这是由政府强制推行的。当政府干预这样一种情况并让人们以某种方式表现或做事时，这真的管用吗？

sentences.en: If nothing changes in the dynamic between two people, being told that they've got to cool off and wait a bit longer, I don't think is going to make them suddenly realise that they want to be together.
sentences.zh: 如果两个人之间的动态关系没有任何改变，被告知他们必须冷静下来并多等一会儿，我认为这不会让他们突然意识到他们想要在一起。

sentences.en: It might be an idea for states to invest in communication programmes for these couples ‘cause that's invariably why relationships fall apart.
sentences.zh: 对于政府来说，投资这些夫妻的沟通项目可能是一个好主意，因为这总是关系破裂的原因。

sentences.en: In response to rising divorce rates, in 2021 the Chinese government introduced a 30-day cooling-off period for couples wanting to separate.
sentences.zh: 为了应对不断上升的离婚率，中国政府在2021年为想要分居的夫妻引入了30天的冷静期。

sentences.en: A cooling-off period is a period of time in which two groups who are arguing can try to improve the situation before taking further action.
sentences.zh: 冷静期是指发生争执的两组人在采取进一步行动之前，可以尝试改善局势的一段时间。

sentences.en: However, it’s unusual for governments to intervene - to become involved - in people’s private lives this way.
sentences.zh: 然而，政府以这种方式干预——介入——人们的私生活是不寻常的。

sentences.en: Joanna doubts a cooling-off period will work, especially as the main reason for relationships failing is non-communication.
sentences.zh: Joanna怀疑冷静期是否会起作用，特别是由于关系破裂的主要原因是缺乏沟通。

sentences.en: She says a lack of communication is invariably - or always - the reason for divorce.
sentences.zh: 她说，缺乏沟通总是——或者一直是——离婚的原因。

sentences.en: On the plus side, by communicating openly, maybe with the professional help of a relationship counsellor, saving a marriage is possible.
sentences.zh: 好的一面是，通过公开沟通，也许在婚姻顾问的专业帮助下，挽救婚姻是可能的。

sentences.en: I think it’s time you reveal the answer to your question, Phil.
sentences.zh: 我想是时候揭晓你问题的答案了，Phil。

sentences.en: You asked about ‘Divorce Day’ in Britain, and I guessed it was the first Monday of the new year.
sentences.zh: 你问的是英国的“离婚日”，我猜是新年的第一个星期一。

sentences.en: Good guess Georgie, because that’s the correct answer!
sentences.zh: 猜得好，Georgie，因为那是正确答案！

sentences.en: ‘Divorce Day’ is the first Monday of the year.
sentences.zh: “离婚日”是新年的第一个星期一。

sentences.en: OK, let’s recap the vocabulary we’ve learned in this programme, starting with stay-at-home mum, a phrase for a woman who stays home to care for her children and manage the household.
sentences.zh: 好的，让我们回顾一下我们在本节目中学到的词汇，首先是“全职妈妈”（stay-at-home mum），这是一个用来形容呆在家里照顾孩子和打理家务的女性的短语。

sentences.en: If you change your mind, you change an earlier decision you made or opinion you had.
sentences.zh: 如果你改变了主意（change your mind），你就会改变之前做出的决定或持有的观点。

sentences.en: If a problem is unresolvable, it cannot be satisfactorily solved or fixed.
sentences.zh: 如果一个问题是无法解决的（unresolvable），它就无法得到圆满的解决或修复。

sentences.en: A cooling-off period is a period of time for two people to try to resolve their differences.
sentences.zh: 冷静期（cooling-off period）是两个人试图解决他们分歧的一段时间。

sentences.en: It can also mean an agreed length of time in which someone can change their mind about something they’ve agreed to buy.
sentences.zh: 它也可以指某人可以改变他们同意购买某物的主意的商定时间长度。

sentences.en: To intervene means to become involved in a difficult situation in order to improve it.
sentences.zh: 干预（intervene）意味着卷入一个困难的局面以便改善它。

sentences.en: And finally, the adverb invariably means always.
sentences.zh: 最后，副词“总是”（invariably）的意思是始终。

sentences.en: Once again our six minutes are up, but remember to join us again next time for more trending topics and useful vocabulary.
sentences.zh: 我们的六分钟又到了，但请记得下次再次加入我们，了解更多热门话题和有用的词汇。

sentences.en: Goodbye for now! Bye!
sentences.zh: 先说再见啦！拜拜！
